audit.title: Cryptocurrency Data Streams
audit.summary: This is a reference index page whose entire value — the catalog of crypto stream names, IDs, and network verifier addresses — is client-side rendered and appears in the served markup only as `Loading...`. The measured facts confirm this: 90 words total, 0 tables, 0 bullets, 0 numerals, 0 hex identifiers. The single biggest strength is clean, valid `TechArticle` + `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD and a correct canonical; the single biggest opportunity — dominating everything else — is that a generative engine or agent fetching this page retrieves almost no substantive content and cannot see a single stream ID. Honest verdict: the schema is agent-ready but the body is not, so this page will be under-cited relative to its actual authority as *the* canonical source for Chainlink crypto stream IDs.

recommendations.title: Server-render (or statically embed) the stream catalog
recommendations.mapsTo: concrete specifics, answer-first extractability, query coverage
recommendations.where: `## Mainnet Crypto Streams` section (currently renders as `Loading...`)
recommendations.issue: `Loading...` — the entire ID table is client-side only.
recommendations.change: Emit the stream table (asset pair, stream ID, verifier network, address) as static HTML/markdown in the served response, or provide an SSR fallback. Even a `<noscript>` table would let crawlers and LLMs read the IDs.
recommendations.why: Retrieval is the dominant loss; a page that returns 90 words and no IDs cannot be cited for the facts it exists to provide. This single change unlocks dimensions 1, 3, and 8 simultaneously.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first lead sentence with a canonical definition
recommendations.where: Directly under the H1, before the top-of-book caveat.
recommendations.issue: Page opens with an edge-case caveat, not a definition.
recommendations.change: Add: "Chainlink Cryptocurrency Data Streams provide high-frequency, low-latency market data for crypto asset pairs, each identified by a unique stream ID and verifiable onchain. This page lists every available crypto stream, its ID, and its verifier network." Then keep the top-of-book note.
recommendations.why: Gives engines a liftable, self-contained definition and states the page's purpose in the first chunk.

recommendations.title: Phrase a section/heading around symptom and lookup queries
recommendations.issue: No heading matches "how do I find a stream ID for X."
recommendations.change: Add an H2 such as "How to find a crypto stream ID and verifier address" and one line pointing to the filterable table and the discovery endpoint.
recommendations.why: Headings phrased as the actual lookup question win retrieval that a bare catalog loses.

recommendations.title: Fix the auto-generated schema `keywords` and `about`
recommendations.issue: `"keywords":"list, available, Data, Streams, crypto, streams, and, their, ID."` and templated `about` ("Content about data").
recommendations.change: Replace with meaningful entities: `"Chainlink Data Streams, crypto price feeds, stream ID, verifier proxy, onchain report verification"`; set `about` names/descriptions to real concepts.
recommendations.why: Aids entity resolution; the current tokens include a stopword and legitimize nothing. Low effort.

recommendations.title: Emit a real `dateModified`
recommendations.change: Wire `dateModified` to the catalog's last content update so freshness reflects when streams were added/changed.
recommendations.why: A catalog that changes should show it; visible freshness is a trust/E-E-A-T signal for a list that agents must trust as current.

recommendations.title: Add one concrete worked example inline
recommendations.where: After the intro, before the table.
recommendations.issue: No example stream ID or usage anywhere on the page.
recommendations.change: Show one full row in prose, e.g. "For example, the ETH/USD stream ID is `0x000...` on Arbitrum Mainnet (verifier proxy `0x...`)." with a link to the fetch/decode tutorial.
recommendations.why: A single concrete, hex-bearing example is highly liftable and survives even if the dynamic table fails to render.

antiPatterns: **Wall-behind-JavaScript:** primary content served as `Loading...`; the most severe issue here.
**Auto-generated metadata cruft:** `keywords` contain a stopword ("and") and tokenized fragments; `about` entries use the "Content about X" template.
No keyword stuffing or marketing fluff detected in the prose itself.
offPageNotes: Confirm `docs.chain.link` exposes an `llms.txt` and that this catalog (or its API discovery endpoint) is listed there, so agents can find stream IDs via a machine-readable route independent of JS rendering.

Consider linking this page prominently from the Data Streams hub and tutorial pages as the canonical stream-ID reference (canonical-hub pattern) to consolidate citations here rather than on aggregator pages.
The CLI passed `<head>` — metadata was fully verified; the empty body reflects genuine client-side rendering, not a fetch artifact.
